claims.text: The initial equiatomic FeCoNiCrMn alloy is a homogenized, single-phase material with no detectable precipitates.
The proposed intervention is aging at approximately 600°C for 2 hours in an inert atmosphere followed by rapid quenching.
The aging treatment will produce a uniform distribution of nanoscale coherent precipitates in equiatomic FeCoNiCrMn.
The precipitates may be Ni-rich or Cr-rich clusters.
The nanoscale coherent precipitates will serve as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
The precipitates will create local variations in magnetic anisotropy.
Precipitate-induced anisotropy variations will hinder magnetic domain-wall motion.
Hindering domain-wall motion will increase coercivity relative to a precipitate-free baseline.
An inert atmosphere is required to prevent oxidation during aging.
Careful control of aging temperature and time is required to form uniformly distributed nanoscale precipitates.
The aged sample should exhibit a statistically significant increase in coercive field relative to a homogenized, unaged baseline.
The homogenized, unaged baseline lacks nanoscale precipitates.
Deviations from the aging parameters could produce nonuniform precipitates or unwanted phases.
Nonuniform precipitates or unwanted phases could reduce the coercivity enhancement.
The magnitude of the coercive-field increase may depend sensitively on precipitate size and distribution and on the exact aging parameters.
